newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-SOLID START BY NZ IN 1ST TEST VS SRI LANKA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOLID START BY NZ IN 1ST TEST VS SRI LANKA.

text.p: New Zealand made a promising start to their innings in the first session of their first cricket test against Sri Lanka at Dunedin on Friday.
Asked to bat after Sri Lanka won the toss, New Zealand were comfortably placed at 92 for one at lunch, with opener Bryan Young on 41 and Matt Horne on 17.
The only wicket to fall was that of Young's opening partner Blair Pocock, who was caught at first slip by Roshan Mahanama off the bowling of left arm seamer Chaminda Vaas for 18.
Young and Pocock had put on 55 for the first wicket before Horne came to the crease and immediately looked to dominate.

After offering no stroke to a seaming delivery from Vaas which shaved his off stump, Horne drove the Sri Lankan down the ground for four and later executed a fine hook shot which brought him six runs over backward square leg off the same bowler.

Young played and missed often in cloudy, overcast conditions which favoured the bowlers, but he interspersed the poor shots with a number of good ones, most notably when he stroked Vaas to the cover boundary off the back foot seven minutes before the lunch break.
The Sri Lankans were unlucky not to have more success. Vaas and fellow left arm fast bowler Nuwan Zoysa proved a handful at times as they got the ball to seam back into the right-handed batsmen.
Zoysa, 18, impressed in his test debut, often troubling the batsmen with exacting deliveries.
New Zealand had a setback before play started when fast bowler Geoff Allott pulled out of the game because of a back injury.
